stem: Meera reads in her school library book that astronomers have found a planet revolving around a star far outside our Solar System. Her friend Arjun asks what such a planet is called and where it belongs. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It is an exoplanet, and it lies in a galaxy beyond the Solar System.
It is a galaxy, because any planet revolving around another star is called a galaxy.
It is part of the Solar System, because every planet must revolve around our Sun.
It is proof that life exists there, because finding a planet means life has been found on it.

teacher.key_rationale: An exoplanet is a planet orbiting a star other than the Sun, so it lies beyond the Solar System within a galaxy; B wrongly equates a planet with a galaxy (term substitution trap), C wrongly places it inside the Solar System (scope/relationship trap), and D wrongly treats discovery of an exoplanet as evidence of life, which is not yet known.
